what_happened: The agent running Athena told Sri on 14 Nov that planning makes things worse. It was repeating a reviewer's week-over-week comparison. It had not checked planned against unplanned jobs in the same period. A same-period check of the records showed planned code jobs in November landing at 65% against 45% for unplanned jobs. The figure is 73% once jobs get past planning. Planning costs about 3x per landing. No job work was judged.
cause: The agent reports on shared state without resolving what it refers to, and Athena does not guard it. Here the state was a claim about planning's effect on landing rates. Athena has no standing same-period figure for planned and unplanned jobs. A reviewer's week-over-week comparison therefore reads like a finding, and nothing ties a claim about system performance to a check of the records. The only guard is the agent's own habit of checking the records first.
other_causes: The reviewer's comparison compared different weeks and different work, and nothing marked it as confounded when it was passed on.
open_hypotheses: Whether the 65% and 45% landing rates are themselves confounded, for example by job size or type. The fields do not say.
prevention: Add an `athena` stage-effect command. It would print landing rate and cost per landing for planned and unplanned jobs over the same window, split by work type and counted from the records. Any claim that a stage helps or hurts would be made from its output. The agent's notes would also say to run it before relaying a comparison from a reviewer.
proposed_request: Add a read-only command, `athena stage-effect`, that reports for a chosen date window the landing rate and cost per landing of planned and unplanned code jobs, split by work type. It must also show the rate for jobs that got past planning, and it must flag any comparison whose groups cover different periods. Acceptance: (1) run over November 2026 records it reports figures that match a hand count of the job records; (2) it works when one group is empty and says so; (3) a test covers the planned, unplanned and empty cases using the recorded job shapes; (4) a CHANGELOG.md entry is included.
